title: Why 0.1 + 0.2 isn't 0.3 (it's not a bug)
description:
Python says 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004. Here's why your computer does this, what it actually stores, and the one rule that avoids the bug.

#coding #python #computerscience #shorts
angle: Your computer isn't wrong about 0.1 + 0.2; it can't store 0.1 exactly, the same way decimal can't store one third.
hook: Python says zero point one plus zero point two is not zero point three.

scenes.narration: Python says zero point one plus zero point two is not zero point three.
Is Python broken? No. Your computer just counts in base two.
In decimal, one third never ends. In binary, zero point one never ends either.
So the computer stores a rounded copy. Here is what zero point one really is, inside.
Two tiny errors add up, and suddenly you can see the mistake.

props.text: tiny error + tiny error = visible bug

scenes.narration: So never compare floats with double equals. Ask if they are close enough.
Close enough. That is the whole trick.

claims.text: 0.1 + 0.2 evaluates to 0.30000000000000004 in IEEE 754 double precision
math.isclose uses a default relative tolerance of 1e-09
